chunks: Ḥammād narrated from al-Ḥalabī, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام.
He was asked about a man who buys a garment from the market for his family and takes it on a condition, then is given profit concerning his family.

He said: “If he desires the profit, then let him make the garment binding upon himself, and let him not place within himself the intention to return the garment to its owner if it is returned to him.”

key_terms.الثَّوْبَ: the garment being purchased and discussed in the transaction
key_terms.بِشَرْطٍ: upon a condition, referring to a conditional arrangement in the sale
key_terms.صَاحِبِهِ: its owner, meaning the original seller or holder of the garment
key_terms.فَلْيُوجِبِ: let him make it binding, meaning to firmly conclude the purchase upon himself

ai.seo_question: When is it permissible to take profit on a garment bought for one's family with a return condition?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about taking profit in a garment purchase made for one's family. The profit is only appropriate if the buyer truly commits himself to the purchase and does not internally intend to return the item to its original owner if his family rejects it.
